records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, go to Pharaoh and speak to him, thus says Yahweh, [the] God of the Hebrews, let go my people that they may serve me.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, says this: Release {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so they can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and speak to him, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews: Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, that they may serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and tell him, 'Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go so they can worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: the God of the Hebrews: the title Moses was given for speaking to Pharaoh
decisions.reason: God gave Moses this title in 3:18, and it is used before Pharaoh in 5:3 and 7:16, and again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: serve: work for, worship
decisions.reason: The verb means both to work for a master and to worship. Israel is to be released from serving Pharaoh (1:13-14) in order to serve God (7:16, 26; 8:16).

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in 7:16, Readable uses "worship", the sense of "serve" that fits a journey to sacrifice; Literal and Balanced keep "serve".

records.heading: Disease strikes the livestock

records.source: כִּ֛י אִם־מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לְשַׁלֵּ֑חַ וְעוֹדְךָ֖ מַחֲזִ֥יק בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: For if refusing [are] you to let go, and still you [are] holding on to them,
pieces: If you refuse to let them go and keep your grip on them,

L.2: For if you refuse to let [them] go and are still holding on to them,

R.2: If you refuse to let them go and keep holding on to them,

decisions.choice: holding on to them: keeping a firm grip, holding fast
decisions.reason: The verb is from the root "be strong", the same root used for Pharaoh's strong heart (4:21; 7:13; verse 12). Pharaoh's grip on Israel and his set will are described with one root.

decisions.choice: for if: the condition whose result follows in verse 3
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 3, which says what will happen if Pharaoh refuses.

records.source: הִנֵּ֨ה יַד־יְהוָ֜ה הוֹיָ֗ה בְּמִקְנְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּסּוּסִ֤ים בַּֽחֲמֹרִים֙ בַּגְּמַלִּ֔ים בַּבָּקָ֖ר וּבַצֹּ֑אן דֶּ֖בֶר כָּבֵ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: look, [the] hand of Yahweh [is] about to be on your livestock which [is] in the field, on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the cattle, and on the sheep, [a] pestilence very heavy.
pieces: then the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will fall on your animals out in the fields, on your horses, donkeys, and camels, your cattle and your sheep, with a very severe disease.

L.3: look, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is about to be upon your livestock that are in the field, upon the horses, upon the donkeys, upon the camels, upon the cattle, and upon the sheep: a very heavy pestilence.

R.3: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will use {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power against your animals out in the fields. Your horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, and sheep will get a terrible disease.

decisions.choice: the hand of Yahweh: Yahweh's power acting against them
decisions.reason: God said in 3:20 that he would stretch out his hand and strike Egypt. Here Moses speaks for God and names him in the third person.

decisions.choice: pestilence: a deadly disease
decisions.reason: The word is used of plague or epidemic disease, among animals here and among people in verse 15 and 5:3.

decisions.choice: very heavy: very severe
decisions.reason: The adjective is from the root "heavy", used of Pharaoh's heavy heart (7:14; verse 7) and of the hail in verses 18 and 24.

decisions.choice: will use his power against
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's hand.

records.source: וְהִפְלָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה בֵּ֚ין מִקְנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבֵ֖ין מִקְנֵ֣ה מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹ֥א יָמ֛וּת מִכָּל־לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And will distinguish Yahweh between [the] livestock of Israel and between [the] livestock of Egypt, and not will die of all [that belongs] to [the] sons of Israel anything.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will set Israel's livestock apart from Egypt's, and not one animal that belongs to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will die.'"

L.4: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will distinguish between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, and nothing of all that belongs to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel will die.'"

R.4: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will treat the animals of Israel differently from the animals of Egypt. Not one animal that belongs to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will die.'"

decisions.choice: distinguish: set apart, treat differently
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Goshen and the flies in 8:18 and of the last plague in 11:7.

decisions.choice: not ... anything: not a single animal
decisions.reason: The negative with "anything" at the end of the sentence is emphatic: none at all. Verse 6 reports it happening.

records.source: וַיָּ֥שֶׂם יְהוָ֖ה מוֹעֵ֣ד לֵאמֹ֑ר מָחָ֗ר יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And set Yahweh [an] appointed time, saying, tomorrow will do Yahweh this thing in the land.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} fixed a time and said, "Tomorrow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do this in the land."

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set an appointed time, saying, "Tomorrow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do this thing in the land."

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chose a time. He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will do this in the land tomorrow."

decisions.choice: an appointed time: a set time
decisions.reason: Naming the time in advance showed that the plague was not chance (compare 8:19). It also gave Pharaoh a day in which to listen.

decisions.choice: Yahweh will do: God speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: The announcement names Yahweh in the third person, as in verses 3-4, as a message to be passed on to Pharaoh.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיָּ֕מָת כֹּ֖ל מִקְנֵ֣ה מִצְרָ֑יִם וּמִמִּקְנֵ֥ה בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹא־מֵ֥ת אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And did Yahweh this thing from the next day, and died all [the] livestock of Egypt, and of [the] livestock of [the] sons of Israel not died one.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} carried this out on the following day. Egypt's livestock all died, but of the livestock of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} not one animal was lost.

L.6: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of Egypt died, but of the livestock of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel not one died.

R.6: On the next day, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did just what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said. The animals of the Egyptians all died. But not even one animal of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} died.

decisions.choice: all the livestock of Egypt: the animals in the fields, a vast number
alternatives: every animal in Egypt without exception
decisions.reason: Egyptian livestock appear again in verses 19-21 and 25 and at the last plague (11:5; 12:29). "All" is most likely a sweeping way of describing a vast loss, or it means all the animals in the field, where verse 3 said the disease would strike.

decisions.choice: not one died: the distinction of verse 4 kept exactly
decisions.reason: The sentence sets the two herds side by side: Egypt's died, Israel's did not lose one.

decisions.choice: did just what he had said
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this thing" was: the plague announced in verses 3-5.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֗ה לֹא־מֵ֛ת מִמִּקְנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־אֶחָ֑ד וַיִּכְבַּד֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־הָעָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And sent Pharaoh, and look, not had died of [the] livestock of Israel even one. And was heavy [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he let go the people.
pieces: Pharaoh sent men to look into it, and indeed not a single animal of Israel's livestock had died. Yet Pharaoh stayed stubborn and did not release the people.

L.7: And Pharaoh sent, and look, not even one of the livestock of Israel had died. But the heart of Pharaoh was heavy, and he did not let the people go.

R.7: Pharaoh sent men to find out what had happened. They found that not even one of the animals of Israel had died. But Pharaoh was still stubborn. He would not let the people go.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh sent: sent messengers to find out
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; the context shows that Pharaoh sent people to see whether Israel's animals had died.

decisions.choice: the heart was heavy: Pharaoh's will stayed dull and unmoved
decisions.reason: The verb is from the root "heavy" (7:14; 8:11, 28); see the note on the three verbs at 7:3. Even proof of the distinction does not move him.

decisions.choice: stayed stubborn / was still stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "was heavy"; Balanced and Readable say what a heavy heart means here.

decisions.choice: sent men to look into it / sent men to find out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom Pharaoh sent and why; Readable also says "They found".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֒ קְח֤וּ לָכֶם֙ מְלֹ֣א חָפְנֵיכֶ֔ם פִּ֖יחַ כִּבְשָׁ֑ן וּזְרָק֥וֹ מֹשֶׁ֛ה הַשָּׁמַ֖יְמָה לְעֵינֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron, take for yourselves [the] fullness of your hollowed hands [of] soot of [a] kiln, and will throw it Moses toward the heavens before [the] eyes of Pharaoh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron, "Fill both your hands with soot from a kiln, and let Moses throw it up toward the sky in Pharaoh's sight.

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and to Aaron, "Take for yourselves your hands full of soot from a kiln, and let Moses throw it toward the heavens before the eyes of Pharaoh.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron, "Scoop up handfuls of black soot from a hot kiln. Moses must throw it up into the air while Pharaoh is watching.

decisions.choice: soot of a kiln: ash or soot from a furnace
decisions.reason: The first word is found only here and in verse 10; it means soot or fine ash. A kiln was a furnace for firing pottery, bricks or lime; its smoke is a picture of destruction in Genesis 19:28 and of the smoking mountain in 19:18.

decisions.choice: the fullness of your hollowed hands: as much as both cupped hands can hold
decisions.reason: The word means the hollow of the hand. The same expression is used of handfuls of incense in Leviticus 16:12.

decisions.choice: throw: toss or scatter
decisions.reason: The verb is used of tossing blood against the altar (24:6). Moses is to fling the soot into the air where Pharaoh can see it.

records.heading: Boils

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה לְאָבָ֔ק עַ֖ל כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהָיָ֨ה עַל־הָאָדָ֜ם וְעַל־הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה לִשְׁחִ֥ין פֹּרֵ֛חַ אֲבַעְבֻּעֹ֖ת בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it will become fine dust over all [the] land of Egypt, and it will become on man and on beast boils breaking out [in] blisters in all [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: It will turn into fine dust over the whole land of Egypt, and all through the land it will become boils, bursting into blisters on people and on animals."

L.9: And it will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will become, upon humans and upon animals, boils breaking out [in] blisters in all the land of Egypt."

R.9: The soot will turn into fine dust that spreads over all of Egypt. It will cause boils on people and animals everywhere in Egypt. The boils will break out into blisters."

decisions.choice: boils: inflamed swellings of the skin
decisions.reason: The word is used of a skin disease: "the boils of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 28:27, 35), Job's sores (Job 2:7) and Hezekiah's illness (2 Kings 20:7). The exact disease cannot be identified.

decisions.choice: breaking out in blisters: boils that erupt into open sores
decisions.reason: The word for blisters is found only here and in verse 10. It may mean pustules, swellings full of fluid, or open sores; "breaking out" is the verb for something bursting or sprouting.

decisions.choice: fine dust: powdery dust carried on the wind
decisions.reason: The word is used of the dust a chariot or a wind raises (Ezekiel 26:10; Deuteronomy 28:24). The handfuls of soot spread across the whole land.

decisions.choice: The soot
decisions.reason: Readable names what "it" is.

records.source: וַיִּקְח֞וּ אֶת־פִּ֣יחַ הַכִּבְשָׁ֗ן וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיִּזְרֹ֥ק אֹת֛וֹ מֹשֶׁ֖ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יְמָה וַיְהִ֗י שְׁחִין֙ אֲבַעְבֻּעֹ֔ת פֹּרֵ֕חַ בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they took the soot of the kiln and stood before Pharaoh, and threw it Moses toward the heavens, and it became boils, blisters, breaking out on man and on beast.
pieces: They took the kiln soot and went to stand in front of Pharaoh. When Moses threw it up toward the sky, it became boils, breaking out in blisters on people and animals alike.

L.10: And they took the soot of the kiln and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses threw it toward the heavens, and it became boils [with] blisters breaking out upon humans and upon animals.

R.10: Moses and Aaron took the soot and stood in front of Pharaoh. Moses threw it up into the air. Then boils broke out on people and animals and turned into blisters.

decisions.choice: the soot of the kiln: the soot God had named
decisions.reason: The article points back to verse 8. They did exactly as they were told.

decisions.choice: Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are, from verse 8.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֣וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֗ים לַעֲמֹ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִפְּנֵ֣י הַשְּׁחִ֑ין כִּֽי־הָיָ֣ה הַשְּׁחִ֔ין בַּֽחֲרְטֻמִּ֖ם וּבְכָל־מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And not were able the magicians to stand before Moses because of the boils, for were the boils on the magicians and on all Egypt.
pieces: The boils kept the magicians from even appearing before Moses, for they had the boils, as did all the Egyptians.

L.11: And the magicians were not able to stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the magicians and on all Egypt.

R.11: The magicians could not even come to face Moses. They had boils too, just like all the other Egyptians.

decisions.choice: stand before Moses: appear before him, hold their ground against him
decisions.reason: The magicians stood against Moses and copied the first signs (7:11, 22; 8:3), failed at the gnats (8:14-15), and now cannot even appear. This is the last time they are mentioned in Exodus.

decisions.choice: all Egypt: all the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The country's name stands for its people.

decisions.choice: even
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "even" to bring out how far the magicians have fallen since 7:11.

records.source: וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק יְהוָה֙ אֶת־לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: And made strong Yahweh [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he listened to them, just as had said Yahweh to Moses.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, however, hardened the heart of Pharaoh, who refused to listen to them, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses.

L.12: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the heart of Pharaoh strong, and he did not listen to them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to Moses.

R.12: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh stubborn. Pharaoh would not listen to Moses and Aaron. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses this would happen.

decisions.choice: Yahweh made the heart of Pharaoh strong: the first time the narrator says God did it
decisions.reason: God said he would do this (4:21; 7:3). Until now the narrator has said that Pharaoh's heart "was strong" (7:13, 22; 8:15) or that Pharaoh made it heavy (8:11, 28). Here, for the first time, Yahweh is the subject, as he said he would be. The verb is "make strong"; see the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh had said to Moses: God's word in 4:21 and 7:3-4
decisions.reason: God told Moses before the signs began that he would strengthen Pharaoh's heart and that Pharaoh would not listen.

decisions.choice: hardened / made Pharaoh stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "made strong"; Balanced and Readable say what a strong heart means here.

decisions.choice: Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, rise early in the morning and present yourself before Pharaoh, and say to him, thus says Yahweh, [the] God of the Hebrews, let go my people that they may serve me.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Be up early in the morning and take your stand in front of Pharaoh. Tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, says this: Release {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so they can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.13: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh, and say to him, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews: Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, that they may serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning. Go and stand in front of Pharaoh and tell him, 'Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go so they can worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: rise early and station yourself: the third meeting of this kind
decisions.reason: Moses is again to meet Pharaoh early in the morning, as at 7:15 and 8:16. The demand is the same as in verse 1.

decisions.choice: serve: work for, worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, Readable uses "worship" for "serve".

records.heading: A warning of hail

records.source: כִּ֣י׀בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֗את אֲנִ֨י שֹׁלֵ֜חַ אֶת־כָּל־מַגֵּפֹתַי֙ אֶֽל־לִבְּךָ֔ וּבַעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וּבְעַמֶּ֑ךָ בַּעֲב֣וּר תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין כָּמֹ֖נִי בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: For at this time I [am] about to send all my plagues to your heart and on your servants and on your people, so that you may know that there [is] none like me in all the earth.
pieces: For now I will aim all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plagues at your very heart, and at your officials and your people. Then you will learn that in the whole world there is none like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.14: For this time I am sending all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plagues to your heart, and upon your servants and upon your people, so that you may know that there is none like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in all the earth.

R.14: This time I will send all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plagues to strike you, your officials, and your people. Then you will know that nobody in all the world is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: all my plagues to your heart: the plagues aimed at Pharaoh himself
decisions.reason: "Heart" may mean Pharaoh's own person, so that the plagues will strike him and not only his land; or it may mean his will, the heart that has been hard, which the plagues are meant to reach. "All my plagues" points to the full series still to come.

decisions.choice: none like me in all the earth: Yahweh has no equal anywhere
decisions.reason: Moses said in 8:6 that there is none like Yahweh. Israel sings it after the sea is crossed (15:11).

decisions.choice: to strike you
decisions.reason: Readable says the plagues will strike Pharaoh himself and leaves out the picture of the heart.

decisions.choice: your officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21; 8:5). Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

records.source: כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֶת־יָדִ֔י וָאַ֥ךְ אוֹתְךָ֛ וְאֶֽת־עַמְּךָ֖ בַּדָּ֑בֶר וַתִּכָּחֵ֖ד מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: For now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been cut off from the earth.
pieces: I could already have raised {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand and struck you and your people with deadly disease, and you would have disappeared from the earth.

L.15: For by now I could have stretched out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand and struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been cut off from the earth.

R.15: Before this, I could have used {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against you and your people. I could have sent a deadly sickness, and you would be gone from the earth.

decisions.choice: now I could have stretched out: what God might have done but did not
alternatives: now I will stretch out my hand
decisions.reason: The verbs are past in form but describe something that did not happen: by now God could have destroyed Pharaoh. Verse 16 says why he did not.

decisions.choice: pestilence: the same word as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The disease that killed the livestock could have struck the people as well.

decisions.choice: cut off: wiped out, made to disappear
decisions.reason: The verb means to be hidden away or destroyed so that nothing is left.

decisions.choice: used my power against
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's hand.

records.source: וְאוּלָ֗ם בַּעֲב֥וּר זֹאת֙ הֶעֱמַדְתִּ֔יךָ בַּעֲב֖וּר הַרְאֹתְךָ֣ אֶת־כֹּחִ֑י וּלְמַ֛עַן סַפֵּ֥ר שְׁמִ֖י בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: But indeed for this I have caused you to stand: in order to show you my power, and so as to recount my name in all the earth.
pieces: But I have let you survive for this purpose: to show you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power and to have {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name declared throughout the earth.

L.16: But indeed, for this reason I have let you stand: to show you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power, and so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name may be told in all the earth.

R.16: But I have kept you alive for a reason. I wanted to show you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power. And I wanted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to be told all over the world.

decisions.choice: I have caused you to stand: I have let you live, kept you in place
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative of "stand": God has kept Pharaoh standing instead of destroying him (verse 15). Paul quotes this verse in Romans 9:17 with "I raised you up". The Septuagint has "you were preserved".

decisions.choice: that my name may be told in all the earth: God's purpose reaches beyond Egypt
decisions.reason: The nations did hear of it: Rahab in Jericho (Joshua 2:10), the Gibeonites (Joshua 9:9) and the Philistines (1 Samuel 4:8).

decisions.choice: to show you: to let Pharaoh see God's power
alternatives: to show my power in you (Septuagint, Romans 9:17)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "to show you". The Septuagint and Romans 9:17 have "to show in you", Pharaoh as the place where the power is seen.

records.source: עוֹדְךָ֖ מִסְתּוֹלֵ֣ל בְּעַמִּ֑י לְבִלְתִּ֖י שַׁלְּחָֽם׃
records.gloss: Still you [are] exalting yourself against my people, so as not to let them go.
pieces: Even now you raise yourself up against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, refusing to release them.

L.17: Still you are exalting yourself against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so as not to let them go.

R.17: You are still proud, and you stand in the way of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. You will not let them go.

decisions.choice: exalting yourself: setting yourself up, acting proudly
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for a raised road or a siege ramp. Pharaoh lifts himself up against Israel like a barrier in their way.

decisions.choice: still you: a statement, or a question
alternatives: Are you still exalting yourself against my people?
decisions.reason: The sentence can be read as a statement or as an indignant question, "Are you still exalting yourself?" The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: proud ... stand in the way of
decisions.reason: Readable gives both sides of the verb: Pharaoh's pride and his blocking of Israel.

records.source: הִנְנִ֤י מַמְטִיר֙ כָּעֵ֣ת מָחָ֔ר בָּרָ֖ד כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־הָיָ֤ה כָמֹ֨הוּ֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם לְמִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הִוָּסְדָ֖ה וְעַד־עָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] about to rain down about [this] time tomorrow hail very heavy, which not has been like it in Egypt from the day it was founded and until now.
pieces: About this time tomorrow I will rain down hail so heavy that Egypt has seen nothing like it from the day the nation began until now.

L.18: Look, about this time tomorrow I am going to rain down a very heavy hail, such as has not been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.

R.18: So listen! At about this time tomorrow, I will send a terrible hailstorm. Egypt has never had a storm like it, not since the country began.

decisions.choice: very heavy hail: a very severe hailstorm
decisions.reason: The adjective is from the root "heavy", as in verse 3. Pharaoh's heavy heart (verse 7) is met by heavy hail.

decisions.choice: from the day it was founded until now: in all Egypt's history
decisions.reason: The same kind of comparison is used in verse 24 and of the locusts (10:6, 14) and the last cry (11:6).

decisions.choice: rain down: send down from the sky
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God raining fire on Sodom (Genesis 19:24) and manna on Israel (16:4).

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁלַ֤ח הָעֵז֙ אֶֽת־מִקְנְךָ֔ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְךָ֖ בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה כָּל־הָאָדָ֨ם וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה אֲשֶֽׁר־יִמָּצֵ֣א בַשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְלֹ֤א יֵֽאָסֵף֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וְיָרַ֧ד עֲלֵהֶ֛ם הַבָּרָ֖ד וָמֵֽתוּ׃
records.gloss: And now send, bring to safety your livestock and all that [is] to you in the field; all the man and the beast that will be found in the field and not will be gathered to the house, and will come down on them the hail and they will die.
pieces: So now send word to get your livestock and everything you have out in the open under cover. Any person or animal still in the fields and not brought indoors will die when the hail falls on them.'"

L.19: And now send, bring your livestock and all that you have in the field to shelter. Every human and animal that is found in the field and is not gathered into the house, the hail will come down upon them, and they will die.'"

R.19: So send orders right away to bring your animals in from the fields. Bring in everything you have that is out there. The hail will fall on every person and animal still in the fields. Any who have not been brought inside will die.'"

decisions.choice: send, bring to safety: send word to bring them to shelter
decisions.reason: "Send" has no object; Pharaoh is to send an order. The second verb means to bring into a safe place.

decisions.choice: a warning within the judgment
decisions.reason: For the first time God tells the Egyptians how to escape a plague's worst effects. Verses 20-21 show that some of Pharaoh's officials took the warning.

decisions.choice: your livestock: Egyptian animals remain
decisions.reason: Animals are still in Egypt after verse 6; see the note there.

records.source: הַיָּרֵא֙ אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מֵֽעַבְדֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֑ה הֵנִ֛יס אֶת־עֲבָדָ֥יו וְאֶת־מִקְנֵ֖הוּ אֶל־הַבָּתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: The [one] fearing the word of Yahweh of [the] servants of Pharaoh made flee his servants and his livestock into the houses.
pieces: Among Pharaoh's officials, those who feared the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made their servants and their livestock run for the houses.

L.20: Whoever among the servants of Pharaoh feared the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made his servants and his livestock flee into the houses.

R.20: Some of Pharaoh's officials were afraid of what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said. They quickly brought their servants and animals inside.

decisions.choice: feared the word of Yahweh: took Yahweh's warning seriously
decisions.reason: Some of Pharaoh's own court believed the warning, though Pharaoh himself did not yet fear Yahweh (verse 30).

decisions.choice: made flee: hurried them away to safety
decisions.reason: The verb is used of making people or animals flee for refuge (Jeremiah 4:6).

decisions.choice: officials ... servants
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "servants" for both, as the Hebrew uses one word. Balanced and Readable say "officials" for Pharaoh's court and "servants" (style guide) for those who belonged to the officials.

decisions.choice: those who / some of
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the one who feared", meaning each one who did; Balanced and Readable use the plural.

records.source: וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־שָׂ֛ם לִבּ֖וֹ אֶל־דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת־עֲבָדָ֥יו וְאֶת־מִקְנֵ֖הוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And who not set his heart to [the] word of Yahweh, and he left his servants and his livestock in the field.
pieces: Others gave no thought to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and left their servants and livestock out in the open.

L.21: But whoever did not set his heart to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} left his servants and his livestock in the field.

R.21: But others did not pay attention to the warning of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They left their servants and animals out in the fields.

decisions.choice: set his heart: pay attention, take seriously
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of Pharaoh in 7:23: he did not set his heart even to this.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: As in verse 20, "servants" in Balanced and Readable (style guide) for the servants of the officials; Literal keeps "servants".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה נְטֵ֤ה אֶת־יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וִיהִ֥י בָרָ֖ד בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עַל־הָאָדָ֣ם וְעַל־הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וְעַ֛ל כָּל־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that may be hail in all [the] land of Egypt, on man and on beast and on all [the] plant[s] of the field in [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Raise your hand toward the sky so that hail comes down all over the land of Egypt, striking people, animals, and every green plant in Egypt's fields."

L.22: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, so that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, upon humans and upon animals and upon every plant of the field in the land of Egypt."

R.22: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Hold your hand up toward the sky. Then hail will fall all over Egypt. It will fall on the people, the animals, and all the plants in the fields."

decisions.choice: the plants of the field: all green growth, crops and grass
decisions.reason: The word covers the plants people grow and the grass of the open country (Genesis 1:11-12; 2:5). Verses 31-32 say which crops were lost.

decisions.choice: the heavens: the sky
decisions.reason: The same word means the sky above and the heavens; here it is the sky the storm comes from.

records.heading: Hail strikes Egypt

records.source: וַיֵּ֨ט מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶת־מַטֵּהוּ֮ עַל־הַשָּׁמַיִם֒ וַֽיהוָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן קֹלֹת֙ וּבָרָ֔ד וַתִּ֥הֲלַךְ אֵ֖שׁ אָ֑רְצָה וַיַּמְטֵ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בָּרָ֖ד עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And stretched out Moses his staff toward the heavens, and Yahweh gave thunders and hail, and went fire to the earth, and rained Yahweh hail on [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: Moses held his staff up toward the sky, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent out peals of thunder and hail. Lightning streaked down to the earth while {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rained hail on the land of Egypt.

L.23: And Moses stretched out his staff toward the heavens, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave thunder and hail, and fire went down to the earth; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rained hail upon the land of Egypt.

R.23: So Moses held up his staff toward the sky. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made it thunder and hail. Lightning struck the ground. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made hail pour down on the land of Egypt.

decisions.choice: thunder: literally "voices" or "sounds"
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for voice or sound means thunder, as at Sinai (19:16). Thunder is called the voice of Yahweh in Psalm 29:3-9.

decisions.choice: fire went to the earth: lightning struck the ground
decisions.reason: Fire with hail is lightning in the storm, as in Psalm 18:13-14 and 105:32.

decisions.choice: his staff: hand and staff together
decisions.reason: God told Moses to stretch out his hand (verse 22); he did so holding the staff, as with the earlier signs (7:19; 8:1-2).

decisions.choice: lightning
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "fire"; Balanced and Readable say what the fire was.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י בָרָ֔ד וְאֵ֕שׁ מִתְלַקַּ֖חַת בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבָּרָ֑ד כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־הָיָ֤ה כָמֹ֨הוּ֙ בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵאָ֖ז הָיְתָ֥ה לְגֽוֹי׃
records.gloss: And was hail, and fire flashing in [the] midst of the hail, very heavy, which not had been like it in all [the] land of Egypt since it became a nation.
pieces: Hail fell, with lightning flaring through the middle of it. The hail was very heavy, worse than any the whole land of Egypt had known since it became a nation.

L.24: And there was hail, and fire flashing in the midst of the hail, very heavy, such as had not been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.

R.24: Hail fell, and lightning flashed in the middle of the hail. It was a terrible storm. Nothing like it had happened in all of Egypt since it became a country.

decisions.choice: flashing: flaring up again and again
decisions.reason: The verb form, from the verb "take", is used of fire that keeps catching and flaring, as in the storm cloud of Ezekiel 1:4.

decisions.choice: very heavy: describing the hail
decisions.reason: As in verse 18, the hail, not the fire, is "very heavy".

decisions.choice: the land of Egypt: a land with little rain
decisions.reason: Egypt depends on the Nile and has very little rain, so a storm like this was beyond anything its people knew.

decisions.choice: lightning
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

records.source: וַיַּ֨ךְ הַבָּרָ֜ד בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה מֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־עֵ֤שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה֙ הִכָּ֣ה הַבָּרָ֔ד וְאֶת־כָּל־עֵ֥ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה שִׁבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: And struck the hail in all [the] land of Egypt all that [was] in the field, from man and to beast; and all [the] plant[s] of the field struck the hail, and every tree of the field it shattered.
pieces: All across the land of Egypt, whatever was out in the fields, human or animal, was struck by the hail. The hail flattened every plant in the fields and splintered every tree.

L.25: And the hail struck, in all the land of Egypt, all that was in the field, from human to animal; and the hail struck every plant of the field, and it shattered every tree of the field.

R.25: The hail hit everything that was out in the fields in all of Egypt. It hit people and animals. It knocked down all the plants and broke all the trees.

decisions.choice: from man to beast: people and animals alike
decisions.reason: The phrase names both ends of a range and means everything in between.

decisions.choice: shattered: broke in pieces
decisions.reason: The verb is the stronger form of "break": the trees were smashed.

records.source: רַ֚ק בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹ֥א הָיָ֖ה בָּרָֽד׃
records.gloss: Only in [the] land of Goshen, where there [were the] sons of Israel, not was hail.
pieces: Only in the land of Goshen, where the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lived, was there no hail.

L.26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel [were], there was no hail.

R.26: But no hail fell in Goshen, where the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lived.

decisions.choice: only in Goshen: the distinction again
decisions.reason: As with the flies (8:18) and the livestock (verses 4, 6), God spares the place where Israel lives. It happens again with the darkness (10:23).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח פַּרְעֹ֗ה וַיִּקְרָא֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֣ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֖ם חָטָ֣אתִי הַפָּ֑עַם יְהוָה֙ הַצַּדִּ֔יק וַאֲנִ֥י וְעַמִּ֖י הָרְשָׁעִֽים׃
records.gloss: And sent Pharaoh and summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them, I have sinned this time; Yahweh [is] the righteous [one], and I and my people [are] the wicked [ones].
pieces: Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said to them, "I have sinned this time. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is in the right, and the guilt lies with me and my people.

L.27: And Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron and said to them, "I have sinned this time; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] the righteous one, and I and my people [are] the wicked ones.

R.27: Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron. He said to them, "I have sinned this time. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done what is right. My people and I are the ones who have done wrong.

decisions.choice: righteous ... wicked: in the right ... in the wrong
decisions.reason: The two words are the terms of a court case: the righteous party is the one in the right, the wicked party the one found guilty (Deuteronomy 25:1). Pharaoh admits that in this dispute Yahweh is in the right and he and his people are at fault. He does not necessarily confess faith in Yahweh.

decisions.choice: this time: on this occasion
decisions.reason: Pharaoh admits fault for now. The phrase may limit the confession to this one instance, and verse 34 shows it did not last.

decisions.choice: in the right ... the guilt lies with / has done what is right ... have done wrong
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "righteous" and "wicked". Balanced and Readable use the language of a court case to show the sense; "righteous" here is not the Greek key term.

records.source: הַעְתִּ֨ירוּ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְרַ֕ב מִֽהְיֹ֛ת קֹלֹ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים וּבָרָ֑ד וַאֲשַׁלְּחָ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תֹסִפ֖וּן לַעֲמֹֽד׃
records.gloss: Entreat Yahweh, and [there is] enough of being thunders of God and hail; and I will let go you, and not you will continue to stay.
pieces: Plead with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. There has been enough of God's thunder and hail. I will release you. You will stay here no longer."

L.28: Entreat {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for [there has been] enough of the thunder of God and hail. And I will let you go, and you will not stay any longer."

R.28: Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! We cannot take any more of God's thunder and hail. I will let you go. You can leave right away."

decisions.choice: thunder of God: thunder sent by God, or mighty thunder
decisions.reason: Pharaoh most likely means the thunder God is sending. The word for God can also be used to mean "mighty" or "tremendous" (compare "a great city to God" in Jonah 3:3), so the phrase may mean "tremendous thunder".

decisions.choice: entreat: pray on someone's behalf
decisions.reason: The verb of 8:4, 24. Pharaoh asks for prayer a third time.

decisions.choice: you will not continue to stay: you will stay no longer
decisions.reason: Pharaoh promises immediate release, without the limits he set in 8:21, 24.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כְּצֵאתִי֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר אֶפְרֹ֥שׂ אֶת־כַּפַּ֖י אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה הַקֹּל֣וֹת יֶחְדָּל֗וּן וְהַבָּרָד֙ לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶה־ע֔וֹד לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֥י לַיהוָ֖ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And said to him Moses, as I go out [of] the city I will spread out my palms to Yahweh; the thunders will cease, and the hail will not be again, so that you may know that to Yahweh [belongs] the earth.
pieces: Moses replied, "As soon as I am outside the city, I will spread my hands out toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the thunder will end and the hail will be gone, and you will learn that the earth belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.29: And Moses said to him, "When I go out of the city, I will spread out my palms to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth [belongs] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.29: Moses said to Pharaoh, "When I go outside the city, I will raise my hands and pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The thunder and hail will end. Then you will know that the earth belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: spread out my palms: the posture of prayer
decisions.reason: Praying with open hands spread toward heaven is described in 1 Kings 8:22, 38 and Isaiah 1:15. The text does not say why Moses prays outside the city.

decisions.choice: the earth belongs to Yahweh: he rules the whole earth, not only Israel
decisions.reason: The same claim is made in 19:5 and Psalm 24:1. The word can also mean "the land", Egypt itself, but here it most likely means the whole earth, as in verses 14 and 16.

decisions.choice: raise my hands and pray
decisions.reason: Readable says that the gesture is prayer.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֖ה וַעֲבָדֶ֑יךָ יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֚י טֶ֣רֶם תִּֽירְא֔וּן מִפְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And you and your servants, I know that not yet you fear before Yahweh God.
pieces: But you and your officials, I know, have yet to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God."

L.30: But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God."

R.30: But I know this about you and your officials: you still do not fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God."

decisions.choice: Yahweh God: the divine name joined with the word for God
decisions.reason: The pairing is used throughout Genesis 2:4-3:24 but is rare elsewhere in the Pentateuch. Here it may stress that Yahweh, whom Pharaoh has just named (verse 27), is God.

decisions.choice: not yet fear: Pharaoh fears the storm, not Yahweh
decisions.reason: Fear of Yahweh means reverence that obeys (verse 20). Pharaoh has confessed, but Moses knows the confession will not last (verse 34).

decisions.choice: your officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21; 8:5). Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

records.source: וְהַפִּשְׁתָּ֥ה וְהַשְּׂעֹרָ֖ה נֻכָּ֑תָה כִּ֤י הַשְּׂעֹרָה֙ אָבִ֔יב וְהַפִּשְׁתָּ֖ה גִּבְעֹֽל׃
records.gloss: And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley [was in the] ear and the flax [in] bud.
pieces: The flax and barley crops were lost, because the barley had already headed out and the flax had come into flower.

L.31: And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley [was] in the ear, and the flax [was] in bud.

R.31: The hail destroyed the flax, a plant used to make linen cloth, and the barley. The barley plants already had grain on them, and the flax plants had flowers.

decisions.choice: barley in the ear, flax in bud: the time of year
decisions.reason: Verses 31-32 are a note from the narrator. Barley and flax grow faster than wheat and spelt; when barley is in the ear the other grains are still young. The word for the barley's ear gives its name to Abib, the month of the exodus (13:4; 23:15). The hail fell some weeks before that spring month.

decisions.choice: in bud: in flower, forming seed heads
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It may mean that the flax was in bloom or that its seed heads were forming.

decisions.choice: a plant used to make linen cloth
decisions.reason: Readable says what flax is.

decisions.choice: The hail
decisions.reason: Readable names what struck the crops, from verse 25.

records.source: וְהַחִטָּ֥ה וְהַכֻּסֶּ֖מֶת לֹ֣א נֻכּ֑וּ כִּ֥י אֲפִילֹ֖ת הֵֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And the wheat and the spelt not were struck, for late [are] they.
pieces: The wheat and spelt escaped, since they are later crops.

L.32: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they [are] late.

R.32: But the wheat was not hurt. Neither was another kind of wheat called spelt. They come up later in the year.

decisions.choice: spelt: a hardy kind of wheat
decisions.reason: The word names a coarse wheat grown in Egypt and Israel (Isaiah 28:25; Ezekiel 4:9), probably emmer or spelt.

decisions.choice: late: late-ripening
decisions.reason: These grains were still young and low when the hail came, so they were not ruined. The locusts later eat what the hail left (10:5, 15).

decisions.choice: another kind of wheat called spelt
decisions.reason: Readable says what spelt is.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה מֵעִ֤ם פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחְדְּל֤וּ הַקֹּלוֹת֙ וְהַבָּרָ֔ד וּמָטָ֖ר לֹא־נִתַּ֥ךְ אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And went out Moses from with Pharaoh [out of] the city, and spread out his palms to Yahweh, and ceased the thunders and the hail, and rain not was poured out to [the] earth.
pieces: So Moses left Pharaoh and went outside the city, where he spread his hands out toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The thunder and hail came to an end, and the rain stopped pouring onto the ground.

L.33: And Moses went out from Pharaoh, out of the city, and spread out his palms to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and the thunder and the hail ceased, and rain was not poured out upon the earth.

R.33: Moses left Pharaoh and went outside the city. He raised his hands to pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the thunder and hail stopped, and no more rain fell.

decisions.choice: rain was not poured out: the downpour stopped
decisions.reason: Rain is mentioned here for the first time; the storm brought rain as well as hail. The verb is used of pouring out liquid or molten metal.

decisions.choice: spread out his palms: Moses did as he had said
decisions.reason: He keeps the word of verse 29, and the storm ends as he said it would.

decisions.choice: raised his hands to pray
decisions.reason: As in verse 29, Readable says that the gesture is prayer.

records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא פַּרְעֹ֗ה כִּֽי־חָדַ֨ל הַמָּטָ֧ר וְהַבָּרָ֛ד וְהַקֹּלֹ֖ת וַיֹּ֣סֶף לַחֲטֹ֑א וַיַּכְבֵּ֥ד לִבּ֖וֹ ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And saw Pharaoh that had ceased the rain and the hail and the thunders, and he continued to sin, and made heavy his heart, he and his servants.
pieces: Once Pharaoh saw that rain, hail, and thunder had all ceased, he went back to sinning: he hardened his heart, and so did his officials.

L.34: And Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder had ceased, and he sinned again, and he made his heart heavy, he and his servants.

R.34: Pharaoh saw that the rain, hail, and thunder had stopped. Then he sinned once more. He made himself stubborn, and his officials did too.

decisions.choice: he sinned again: Pharaoh goes back on his confession
decisions.reason: Pharaoh said "I have sinned" in verse 27. Breaking his promise is itself sin, as Moses had warned (8:25; 9:30).

decisions.choice: made his heart heavy, he and his servants: the court joins Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The verb from the root "heavy" (see 7:3, 14). For the first time Pharaoh's officials are said to share his hard heart; in 10:1 God says he has made both heavy.

decisions.choice: hardened his heart / made himself stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "made his heart heavy"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: his officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21; 8:5). Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

records.source: וַֽיֶּחֱזַק֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: And was strong [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he let go the sons of Israel, just as had said Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.
pieces: Pharaoh remained stubborn and refused to release the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. It was as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had foretold through Moses.

L.35: And the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not let the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel go, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said by the hand of Moses.

R.35: Pharaoh stayed stubborn. He would not let the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} go. This was just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke through Moses.

decisions.choice: the heart was strong: Pharaoh's will stayed set
decisions.reason: The verb "be strong", as in 7:13, 22 and 8:15; see the note at 7:3. The plague ends as the earlier ones did.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: God's word came to Pharaoh through Moses as his spokesman (4:21; 7:2-4).

decisions.choice: remained stubborn / stayed stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "was strong"; Balanced and Readable say what a strong heart means here.
